answerCheck.reason: For n=2 the numbers are antipodal. For n=3, |z1+z2|²=1 gives Re(z1·conj(z2))=-1/2, and cyclically, forcing 120-degree spacing. Every even n≥4 admits repeated antipodal pairs 1,-1. Every odd n≥5 admits the triple 1,ω,ω² together with antipodal pairs 1,-1. These sums are zero but are not equally spaced, so only two integers qualify.
Since Re(z1 conjugate(z2)) ≤ |z1||z2|, expanding |z1 + z2|² gives at most (|z1| + |z2|)². Taking nonnegative square roots gives B.
Because 1+ω+ω²=0, the corner sums are 0 and ±1, ±ω, ±ω². The linear image of the coefficient cube is their convex hull, a regular hexagon of side 1. Its area is 6(√3/4)=3√3/2.
The segment has length sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5. Its radius-1 neighborhood has area 5·2+π·1^2=10+π, approximately 13.142, whose nearest integer is 13.

Set (u1,u2,u3,u4,u5)=(4-a,a-b,b-c,c-d,d), with sum 4. Since P(1)>0, a unit zero z is not 1. From (z-1)P(z)=0, obtain 4=sum uj·z^(-j). Equality in the unit-circle bound forces z^j=1 whenever uj>0. Thus positive weights are supported within {2,4}, {3}, or {5}. These yield P(1) values 8,10,12,14,16, plus 12 and 20. Their sum is 92.
Set w=z+1/2. Then |w^2+3/4|=4, so |w|^2=|w^2|≤4+3/4=19/4. Hence Im(z)≤√19/2. Equality occurs at w=i√19/2, where w^2+3/4=-4. Thus m+n=19+2=21.
The sum is 2 + 5 = 7, corresponding to (7,0), so its modulus is 7.

answerCheck.reason: |3 + 4i| = √(3² + 4²) = 5; the separate moduli 3 and 4 are not added to obtain the modulus of this sum.

Squaring a_n+i*b_n gives (3+4*i)^n, whose imaginary part is 2*a_n*b_n. Put z=(3+4*i)/7, with modulus 5/7. For every finite N, direct multiplication gives (1-z)*(1+z+...+z^N)=1-z^(N+1). Thus the requested real partial sum is half the imaginary part of (1-z^(N+1))/(1-z). Its remainder has absolute value at most (1/2)*(5/7)^(N+1)/|1-z|, tending to zero by real geometric decay. Finally 1/(1-z)=7/(4-4*i)=7/8+(7/8)*i, yielding 7/16, B. Reuse this complete finite-complex telescope and real remainder route. The real-ratio infinite-series node is used only for its real majorant; its definition is not widened to complex ratios.
